## Scanner, negative coverage and replay

The scanner delta is bounded: an import must full-match Mathlib or one named companion module, stay before the namespace and, for a companion dependency, precede the importing module in MODULES. Self/forward imports fail the order check; root, dotted companion and multi-name imports fail admission. The new open scoped form full-matches capitalized namespace tokens, is checked before ordinary open, and leaves the remaining command/admission checks in force. Root source equality is exact.

The changed tests include positive admissions and intended-reason refusals for self/forward/root/dotted/multi-name imports, import inside the namespace, unknown scanner module, missing/lowercase scoped namespace, appended in/theorem text, indentation and spacing variants. They also refuse the old two-import root, old three-module leanchecker invocation, omitted/reordered module lists, changed successor identities/status, new build failures, altered Census/control source and wrong control outcomes.

An inert AST comparison against 4c33d8cd confirms COMMANDS, TOKEN, ADMISSION, DECLARATION and CENSUS_LINE unchanged. Only metadata, scan_module and check_modules function bodies changed; source, census, finish, negative and exclusive receipt writer remain unchanged. The expanded sets drive the existing fail-closed machinery. The finish fixture's every-member omission loop now covers all 54 members.

The original hosted census is 133 distinct constants: 109 user/range entries exactly equal the inventory, one user/generated entry exactly equal census_auxiliary, and 23 internal/generated entries, with no internal/range entry. This is evidence about these observed modules, not a universal guarantee about declaration-range metadata for every Lean extension. The scanner remains a keyword/shape filter; the Python negative fixtures use placeholder modules and synthetic logs, not compiler execution of adversarial Lean mutations.

replay.sh exports LEAN_NUM_THREADS using ${LEAN_NUM_THREADS:-2}: unset or empty gets 2; a nonempty operator setting survives. Hosted execution already explicitly sets 2. I verified the source change and existing hosted setting, not the author's local unset-variable replay or memory measurements. The 28-test protocol suite does not provide a separate runtime test of that unset-variable branch.
